newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Court rejects Serbian opposition election charge.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects Serbian opposition election charge.

text.p: A court on Wednesday rejected a complaint by the Serbia's Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition that the ruling socialists rigged elections results to deprive it of victory in Belgrade, FoNet news agency reported.
The opposition and student supporters have held 17 days of demonstrations in the capital in protest at the outcome of the elections.
FoNet quoted the Democratic Party, a member of Zajedno, as saying the first municipal court in Belgrade refused to consider new opposition evidence in support of its claim.
Fresh elections would have been possible to settle the conflict between the Zajedno and Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic if the complaint had been upheld.
Milosevic's socialists at first admitted defeat in Belgrade and other towns but later overturned the results, accusing Zajedno of unspecified "irregularities."
Opposition leaders have vowed to continue daily demonstrations in the capital which have attracted up to 100,000 people.
